doc.title: Technical Specification - OpenAI Analysis Layer
doc.snippet: Purpose: Send structured data to OpenAI, get probability estimates. Modules: prompt_builder.py (Story 4.1), client.py (Story 4.2), response_parser.py (Story 4.3). One OpenAI call per fixture, structured JSON input/output, fallback for API failures (mark fixture as "analysis failed").

doc.title: Story 4.1: Build OpenAI Prompt Builder
doc.snippet: Story 4.1 provides `export_prompt_for_api(fixture)` which returns dict with "system_prompt" and "user_message" keys, ready for OpenAI integration. This story integrates Story 4.1 output into OpenAI API calls with retry logic, rate limiting, and error handling.

package.name: openai
package.description: Official OpenAI SDK for async API calls

constraints.constraint: Use official `openai.AsyncOpenAI` client (NOT httpx directly). Per CLAUDE.md, modern OpenAI SDK handles retries automatically for transient errors and provides better structured API interactions.

NEVER use custom error handling for API calls. MUST use existing exception hierarchy: APIAuthenticationError (401/403), APIRateLimitError (429), APIServerError (5xx), OpenAIError (OpenAI-specific). See src/bet_bot/exceptions.py.

MANDATORY: Use tenacity library @retry decorator for retry logic. Pattern exists in src/bet_bot/data/fetchers/api_football.py. Retry conditions: httpx.TimeoutException, httpx.NetworkError, APIServerError (5xx). Do NOT retry 401/403 or 429 (handle separately). Max 3 attempts with exponential backoff (2s, 4s, 8s).

Implement client-side token bucket rate limiter (reference: src/bet_bot/data/fetchers/api_football.py:RateLimiter). Max 500 requests/minute for OpenAI free tier. Respect Retry-After header from 429 responses. Never relay 429 to caller - handle internally with retry.

Use async/await consistently. asyncio.timeout(30) for timeout enforcement (Python 3.11+). asyncio.gather() for batch processing with return_exceptions=True. Never use blocking calls (time.sleep) - use asyncio.sleep().

30s max per fixture analysis. Use asyncio.timeout(30) context manager. On timeout: log ERROR with fixture_id, mark fixture status as "analysis_failed", return fixture with error_message (never raise exception).

Never raise exceptions from analyze_fixture(). On any error: log with context (fixture_id), mark fixture with error status, continue processing other fixtures. Entire run must complete even if one fixture fails.

MUST validate all inputs using Pydantic v2 models. Response from OpenAI must be parsed into AIAnalysis/MarketAnalysis models. Validate probabilities are floats in [0.0, 1.0]. Validate probability sums for multi-outcome markets (e.g., match_result: home+draw+away ≈ 1.0). Log validation failures at WARNING level (don't fail).

Never log API keys (not even masked). Never log full fixture data (log summary only). Log at DEBUG: raw prompt (first 300 chars). Log at INFO: fixture summary, token counts, rate limit waits. Log at WARNING: validation failures, approaching rate limits. Log at ERROR: API failures, timeouts, parsing errors.

Track input_tokens + output_tokens from OpenAI response. Calculate cost: (input_tokens * 0.50 + output_tokens * 1.50) / 1M for GPT-3.5-turbo. Log cumulative cost per run. Warn at INFO level if single fixture > $0.10. Warn at WARNING level if cumulative > $5 threshold.

Add to config.yaml: OPENAI_MODEL (default: "gpt-3.5-turbo"), OPENAI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (default: 30), OPENAI_MAX_RETRIES (default: 3), OPENAI_COST_THRESHOLD (default: 5.0). Validate all config values on startup.

interface.name: OpenAI API - Chat Completions
interface.details: Uses official openai.AsyncOpenAI client to call chat completions endpoint. Request includes system_prompt + user_message from Story 4.1. Response contains JSON with markets array containing type, probabilities, reasoning.

interface.name: analyze_fixture
interface.details: Public API for analyzing single fixture. Accepts consolidated Fixture from Story 3.3. Returns Fixture with ai_analysis field populated (or error_message if failed). Never raises exception.

interface.name: analyze_all_fixtures
interface.details: Batch orchestrator for multiple fixtures. Iterates sequentially (respects rate limits). Returns list of fixtures with analysis attached or error status. Logs progress and summary.

interface.name: export_prompt_for_api
interface.signature: async def export_prompt_for_api(fixture: Fixture) -> dict[str, str]
interface.details: From Story 4.1 (completed). Returns dict with keys: "system_prompt" (str) and "user_message" (str). Called by Story 4.2 analyze_fixture() to get structured prompt before OpenAI API call.

interface.name: Config API
interface.details: Provides API key and configuration values. OPENAI_API_KEY is required (raises ValueError if missing). OPENAI_MODEL defaults to "gpt-3.5-turbo". OPENAI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS defaults to 30.

tests.standards: Project uses pytest for unit and integration testing. All tests use async fixtures with @pytest.mark.asyncio decorator. Mocking uses unittest.mock.patch and pytest-mock for async functions. Tests must have 85%+ code coverage for client.py. Error cases must be tested explicitly (not raising exceptions). Integration tests must use real Story 4.1 prompt_builder output.
tests.locations: tests/unit/test_openai_client.py - unit tests for all client functions and retry logic tests/integration/test_prompt_to_analysis.py - integration tests with Story 4.1 output

ideas.idea: Test valid API key → OpenAIClient created successfully
Test missing OPENAI_API_KEY → raises ValueError with clear message
Test client singleton pattern (second init returns same instance)
Test timeout configuration (30s total, 10s connect)
Test valid fixture → returns fixture with ai_analysis attached
Test fixture with missing fixture_id → logs warning, returns None
Test missing required fields (teams, league) → logs error, returns error fixture
Test fixture from Story 3.3 with quality_score → properly formatted in prompt
Test successful API call → returns Fixture with AIAnalysis
Test response parsing → JSON response correctly mapped to MarketAnalysis objects
Test invalid JSON response → logs error, returns error fixture (no exception)
Test probabilities validation → values > 1.0 clipped with warning
Test probability sum validation → multi-outcome markets (e.g., match_result) sum ≈ 1.0
Test transient failure (timeout) → retries and succeeds (mocked success after 2 attempts)
Test permanent failure (auth error) → no retry, returns error fixture
Test max retries exceeded → returns error fixture (doesn't raise)
Test exponential backoff → waits 2s, 4s, 8s between retries (verify timing)
Test rate limit reached → waits and retries (asyncio.sleep mocked)
Test Retry-After header (seconds) → waits exact duration
Test Retry-After header (HTTP date) → parses and waits correct duration
Test concurrent requests respect token bucket → max 500/min enforced
Test 30s timeout enforced → returns error fixture, not exception
Test timeout during slow API response → logs ERROR, marks analysis_failed
Test APIAuthenticationError (401) → logs CRITICAL, halts with clear message
Test APIRateLimitError (429) → uses rate limiter to wait, retries
Test APIServerError (5xx) → uses tenacity retry logic
Test JSON parse error → logs ERROR, marks analysis_failed
Test unexpected exception → logs EXCEPTION, marks analysis_failed
Test entire run continues if one fixture fails → other fixtures still processed
Test cost calculation for single fixture → (input_tokens * 0.50 + output_tokens * 1.50) / 1M
Test cost exceeding $0.10 per fixture → logs WARNING
Test cumulative cost tracking → sum across multiple fixtures
Test cost threshold warning → logs WARNING when $5 exceeded
Test analyze_all_fixtures with multiple fixtures → processes all sequentially
Test one fixture fails → others continue processing
Test empty fixture list → returns empty list
Test progress logging → "Analyzing fixture X of Y" messages
Test completion summary → "Analyzed X of Y fixtures, Y failures"
Test prompt_to_analysis flow → use export_prompt_for_api() output directly
Test with 3-5 realistic fixtures → verify end-to-end integration
Test response parsing preserves fixture data → original fields unchanged
